PSI U PERSONALITY OF THE MONTH
Howard Christian Naffziger, Epsilon '07
By Stuabt O'Melveny, Epsilon '10
HOWARD
CHRISTIAN NAFFZIGER,
(Eng.) Hon., whose picture painted by Mr.
Seymour Thomas for the American Col
lege of Surgeons is on the inside cover
page of this issue of The Diamond, was
born in Nevada City, California in 1884.
Nevada City is situated amongst the pines
and dogwood on the western
slope of the
Sierra Nevadas. It is one of the most beau
tiful of the old mining towns with a color
ful history in the Gold Rush Days. By 1884
the placer miners had come and gone but
Nevada City, by vhtue of being the county
seat, was far from being a
ghost town.
Amid these pleasant surroundings Howard
Naffziger acquired his early education
graduating from the Nevada City High
School in 1900.
Naffziger did his undergraduate and
pre-medical work at the University of
California situated in Berkeley. At that
time the general educational program of
the University was conducted at
Berkeley
while the medical department and hospi
tal were located in San Francisco. It was
at Berkeley, therefore, that Howard joined
the Epsilon Chapter of the Psi Upsilon.
While he lived in the fraternity house and
took an active interest in the affairs of the
chapter, the seriousness with which he
devoted himself to his medical training
necessitated his absence from most col
lege activities. However, his kindhness,
innate wisdom, and good humor endeared
him to his fraternity brothers so that his
popularity was exceeded by no one.
After leaving Berkeley, Doctor Naffziger
identified himself with the University of
California Hospital in San Francisco as
interne and assistant resident surgeon and
then went on to
spend some time at Johns
Hopkins as assistant resident surgeon. He
returned to the University of Calffornia
Hospital in 1913 and has been identified
with that institution ever since. When
Doctor Naffziger joined the faculty the
development of brain surgery was made
his responsibility and the hospital became
under his guidance the first center of this
type west of the Atlantic seaboard. He
filled various positions on the faculty until
1924 when he was made Clinical Profes
sor of Surgery. In 1929 he became Profes
sor of Surgery and Chairman, Department
of Surgery, of the Medical School, and
Surgeon in Chief of the Hospital. Doctor
Naffziger specializes in neurological sur
gery and when under his guidance a
sepa
rate new
department in this branch was
created in 1947, he became Professor of
Neurological Surgery and Chairman of that
department, which position he still oc
cupies. He is also consulting Surgeon for
the San Francisco Hospital, for the
Langley Porter Clinic, and for the U. S.
Veterans Facihty, San Francisco.
Doctor Naffziger's war record has been
a brilliant one.
During the First World
War he served as Lieutenant Colonel of
the Medical Corps of the United States
Army and was with the American Expedi
tionary Forces. At the conclusion of that
war he accepted a commission as Colonel
in the Medical Reserve Corps, which com
mission he held until 1928. During the
Second World War he was a member of
the .
Surgical Committee of the National
Research Council and Chairrnan of the
Sub-Committee of this Council on Neuro
logical Surgery. He was consultant and
special advisor for the Office of Scientific
Research and Development and was sent
to England and Scotland in 1943, as well
as to the North African Theatre and Mid
dle East to correlate research and as
surgi
cal advisor. After the war he was
ap
pointed Chairman of the Educational Mis
sion to Poland under the auspices of the
UNRRA, visiting London, Paris, Berlin,
and various Pohsh Universities and medi
cal schools.
No biographical account of Doctor
Naffziger would be complete without some

of the many honors which he has re
ceived by reason of his prominence in his
chosen field of neurological surgery.
He is a founder member of the Ameri
can Board of Surgery and has acted as
Chairman of the American Board of Neuro
logical Surgery since its founding in 1939.
He is a Fellow of the American College of
Surgeons and a
Regent since 1934 and was
President ui 1938 and 1939. He is a Fellow
of the Royal College of Surgeons (hon.) of
England. He is a member and past Presi
dent of the San Francisco County Medical
Society; the San Francisco County Neuro
logical Society; California Academy of
Medicine; the Society of Neurological Sur
geons; and is still President of the Pacific
Coast Surgical Association. He is a mem
ber of the American Medical Association;
American Surgical Association; American
Neurological Association; International
Surgical Association; International Neuro
logical Association; Association of Re
search in Nervous and Mental Diseases;
Western Surgical Association; and Hon
orary Consultant to the Library of the
Surgeon General. During the coming No
vember Doctor Naffziger will act as Chair
man of an educational mission to the
Philippines to visit the medical schools.
Doctor Naffziger, in addition to his in
terest in so
many societies and associations,
finds time to serve on the editorial and ad
visory boards of the following medical pe
riodicals: Annals of Surgery; Surgery;
American Journal of Surgery; Western
Journal of Surgery, Geriatrics; Journal of
Neurological Surgery; and Journal of
Neurological Sciences.
Membership in learned societies^ ad
visory "positions on the staff of technical
journals, appointment to government com
missions�all these are the laurels that
crown his career of study and practice. He
has reached that point of eminence which
causes men to look to him for counsel,
but he does not yet think of resting on his
laurels.
In addition to being a member of Psi
Upsilon, he is also a member of Nu Sigma
Nu and Alpha Omega Alpha.
The fact that Doctor Naffziger is one
of the most distinguished surgeons of his
time has in no
way detracted from the
attractiveness of his personality. He is a
very human person. He married Louise
McNear, the daughter of an old and dis
tinguished pioneer family and they have
three daughters and a home filled with
the good things of life. The exactions of
his job have often caused the Doctor to
seek rest and relaxation in inaccessible
places, so his golf has been supplemented
with big game hunting and fishing. High
up in the Sierras Doctor Naffziger has a
summer home and nowhere is he so con
tented as when he is enjoying the music
of the mountain breezes through the pines.
Perhaps they call up memories of his
youth before he scaled the heights.

Theodore P. Gould, Pi '23
Formerly vice-president of Scandinavian
Airlines System, has been appointed di

High School and Syracuse University. He
is married, has a son and two daughters,
and lives at 73 The Intervale, Roslyn, N.Y.
